capabilities: Add or remove a CSS class on the current canvas via commands or settings
Add a CSS class to a closed canvas by its filepath
Rename, remove, or clear CSS classes from the settings
Switch the class append target between the canvas body and workspace leaf
Automatically track canvases when files are moved, renamed, or deleted
extras: The plugin ships no CSS itself; you must write your own rules in the .obsidian/snippets folder. The README explains a trade-off: classes on the workspace leaf survive focus changes but are lost on image export, while body mode does the opposite. The author accepts donations ('coffee money').
intentEvidence: Add the class .canvas-file to the DOM of each canvas file, and adding the attribute [data-canvas-path="filepath"]
problem: Obsidian gives every canvas the same DOM, so you cannot target or style one specific canvas with CSS snippets.
summary: Adds a CSS class and data attributes such as data-canvas-path to canvas files so individual canvases can be styled with your own CSS snippets.
